events.statement: pricing-engine p99 latency was ~60ms until 13:12 and jumped to ~1700-2300ms from the 13:20 bucket onward, then slowly declined.

pricing-engine ERROR logs are dominated by 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms' (72 of 73 matches), with reported downstream times up to 8456ms; first match 13:23:57Z.
market-data-service p99 latency rose from ~40ms to ~1433-1980ms in the same 13:20 bucket, tracking pricing-engine's onset.
market-data-service CPU jumped from ~45% to ~79-94.5% at the 13:20 bucket while memory stayed flat at ~62%, indicating CPU-bound work rather than a memory leak.

market-data-service logs show a 'cache miss storm: quote:<n> not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot (<n>ms)' pattern, 68 occurrences starting 13:22:25Z with rebuild durations up to 8748ms.
redis-cache hit_ratio collapsed from ~96% to 14.8% in the 13:28 bucket while cpu_pct (~22%) and connected_clients (~310) were unchanged, ruling out CPU overload of redis.

redis-cache memory_pct dropped abruptly from ~70% to ~8.6% (max 74.63 at 13:20; avg 8.56 at 13:28) with evictions_per_min flat at ~3/min, indicating the dataset was lost/emptied rather than evicted under pressure.
redis-cache log at 13:22:10Z: 'node redis-cache-2 failed health check (3 consecutive PING timeouts); marking primary as down'.
redis-cache log at 13:22:52Z: 'failover: promoting replica redis-cache-3 to primary; dataset on new primary is empty (replica was resyncing)'.
market-data-service request_rate was stable at ~950-975 req/s across the incident, so the CPU/latency rise is not explained by increased inbound load.
market-data-service and pricing-engine error rates rose from ~0.2% to ~3% and ~4% respectively starting at the 13:20 bucket.
No deployments to pricing-engine or market-data-service on 2026-04-09; the only deployment found was auth-service v7.2.0 at 11:30Z (unrelated to the quote path).
No config/feature-flag changes for any service (0 changes) and none specifically for redis-cache in the incident window.
market-data-service restart counter stayed at 0 throughout, so its latency/CPU rise was not caused by a restart/crashloop.

Historical incident HIST-107 ('Cold cache storm after redis failover') on the same services (redis-cache, market-data-service) had root cause 'Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica' with symptom 'cache miss storm'.
A redis-cache 'client reconnect storm' pattern appears (15048 new connections in 10s at 13:30, 92851 in 10s at 13:40), consistent with clients re-establishing connections after the failover.
